name: BLACK PEARL
blurb: KING-LIKE STEM, OYSTER VIGOUR. TREAT AS ONE FLUSH.

overview.v: Black Pearl, Black King, Black Pearl King, Cosmic Queen and Shimofuri (Hiratake) are used interchangeably.

Best supported: Hokuto Corporation's Shimofuri Hiratake, an interspecific hybrid of P. ostreatus, P. nebrodensis and P. eryngii (Canadian patent CA 2,878,902). Other accounts say European x Asian ostreatus, or king x blue.
Massive king-like stem, softer oyster texture, vigorous even in poorly controlled conditions.
A hybrid that cannot cross within itself, so probably safer than sporing wild types.

cultivation.v: House Master's Mix; no other recipe given.
One 6 lb G2 per twenty 10 lb blocks (about 3%). Do not go beyond 30 blocks per bag.
PDYA. 3-5 days in the flow hood at 27-29 °C, then 18-21 °C. Discard plates older than 3 months.
Slit or cross-cut about 1/4 in (6 mm) deep on the long face. Side-fruiting did as well or better than top-fruiting.
5 mL cryovial, 3 mL of 10% glycerol and 5-10 colonized rye grains, -80 °C.

timeline.v: G2 firm by day 7, usually held to about day 14, then refrigerated. Cold-stored spawn good about 1 month.
Fruitable at about 10 days, stable to 3 weeks. Shipped at 12-13 days.
Full colonisation in about 2 weeks, but heavier blocks after 2.5-3 weeks.
5-7 days after cutting: amber droplets, then pins. Slower than most oysters.

climate.v: Range 10-18 °C, ideal 13-16 °C. 10-12 °C gives the densest fruit. Pinning falls off above about 18 °C.
No number given. Fine high-pressure mist recommended, not coarse fog. An ultrasonic fogger on 30/10 min led to cap yellowing and blotch.
Exhaust fan on at about 800-900 ppm.
Standard full spectrum. Blue LED may help.

yield_.v: 2.58-2.87 lb (1.17-1.30 kg), about 2.7 lb typical. Side-fruited after about 3 weeks.
An estimated +0.5 to +1 lb per block from a longer run plus side fruiting.
One huge "washer" of about 4 lb when CO2 was not controlled.
About 1.15 lb/block aggregate (plan was 1.5), well under the 2.7 lb trial.
Fairly good if picked before the caps flatten. Blocks keep weeks at 1 °C.

hazards.v: Second only to blue oyster. In blocks: very dense, amber-tinted circular patches that predict poor yield.
Lumpy, deformed caps. Water quality blamed almost every time.
Do not keep blocks after the first harvest: exposed wet substrate invites contaminants.

notes.v: Give it an extra week of incubation: cheap insurance for yield.
Inspect grain for hard discoloured spots before spawning. A stroma spot never reverts.
